FOREWORD This 1ndian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Corrosion Protection and Finishes Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council, USC of anticorrosion tapes is one of the various methods employed for protection of the underground from corrosion. Other methods being concrete sheathing, coating and cathodic protection, etc. pipelines

The wrapping tapes can be applied easily over a widely differing range of climatic and site conditions. These tapes provide coating of uniform thickness and weight per unit area of the pipe all around it and are suitable for site repairing of damaged flood-coating on pipe lines also. As such all the hazards associated with flood-coating or conventional coat and wrap methods including the need of tarmelters are avoided in use of these tapes. The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex F

1n reporting of the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value observed OL calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'.

3.2 Coal Tar The coal tar (hard pitch) component shall be produced from coal that has a minimum heating value of 13000 Btu/lb (7.223 x 106 cal/kg) on a moisture and mineral matter free basis and has been carbonized in a slot type coke oven at a temperature of not less than 900�c. Coal tar component shall comply to the requirement as given in Table 2. Table 2 Characteristics of Coal Tar Saturant

The tape made of inorganic fibre shall have glass fibre mat/tissue reinforced with glass yarn. 3.1.1 Inorganic Fibre Fabric (Glass Fibre Mat/Tissue) The inorganic fabric shall be thin, flexible and uniform mat, composed of glass fibre in an open structure bonded with a suitable inert material compatible with coal tar. The mat shall be reinforced with continuous filament glass yarn at approximately 10 mm pitch in the longitudinal direction. The fabric shall conform to the requirements Table 1. given in

IS 15337:2003 5.2 Thickness The tape shall be supplied in the nominal thickness of 2.0 mm, 3.0 mm and 4.0 mm with a tolerance of * 10 percent. 5.2.1 Tapes shall normally be supplied in the nominal thicknesses of 2.0 mm, 3.0 mm or 4 mm. It can however be supplied in thickness other than specified also as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. The tolerance on the nominal thickness shall however be k 10 percent. 5.3 Mass 5.3.1 Mass of the tape expressed in kg/m2 per millimetre of thickness shall be 1.5 kg/m2, with * 10 percent tolerance. 6 APPLICATION OF WRAPPING TAPE 7.2.2 The applied output voltage of the holiday detector shall have a spark discharge of thickness equal to at least twice the thickness of the coating to assure adequate inspection voltage and compensate for any variation in coating thickness. The electrode shall be passed over the coated surface at approximately half the spark discharge distance from the coated surface only one time at the rate of approximately 10 to 20 ndmin. The edge effects shall be ignored. Excessive voltage shall be avoided as it tends to induce holidays in the coated surface thereby giving erroneous readings. 7.2.3 While selecting test voltages, consideration shall be given to the tolerance on coating thickness and the voltage should be selected cm the basis of maximum coating thickness likely to be encountered during testing of a particular pipe. Thickness of Coating mm 2 3 4 Test Voltage, Max kV 10 12 15

For the guidance of users, the recommended practice for application of wrapping tape is given in Annex A. 7 ROUTINE TESTS ON TAPES 7.1 Adhesion Test The temperature of the tape and the pipe to be tested shall be between 10�C and 27"C. If the temperature is outside this range, hot or cold water as required shall be poured over the test area until temperature in the desired range is attained. In addition the adhesion test shall be carried out only after 72 h of curing. The tape shall pass the adhesion test. 7.1.1 Procedure 7.1.1.1 A suitable test area shall be selected where the tape is smooth for 15 cm in longitudinal direction of the tape. 7.1.1.2 Two knife cuts each of 15 cm length shall be made in the tape which are 5 cm apart. 7.1.1.3 A flat blade shall be used to pry up 5 cm long flap. This tlap of fabric shall be grasped firmly in one hand and shall be pulled with a quick motion in the direction of the remaining 10 cm of the 15 cm knife cut. 7.1.1.4 The adhesion shall be deemed satisfactory if the tape tears at the point of stripping or the fabric strips from the underlying coal tar component, leaving exposed the pli med or the bare metal of not more than 10 percent of the total area of the flap adhering, that is, 50 cm2. 7.2 Holiday Test 7.2.1 All coated and wrapped pipes shall be tested with an approved high voltage holiday detector preferably equipped with an audio-visual signaling device to indicate any faults, holes, breaks or conductive particles in the protective coating. 3

7.2.4 The electrical equipment used to test tape wrapping shall be a portable, low amperage, adjustable voltage, pulse type holiday detector. It shall be furnished with a coil spring electrode or,a suitable brush type electrode. The primary input wattage shall not be higher than 20 W and the minimum pulse at crest voltage shall be 20 per second. 7.3 Direct Impact Test This test shall be conducted as per the procedure given in Annex B. 7.4 Corrosion Resistance Test

This shall be carried out as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer at the time of enquiry and order. 7.5 Identification of Tape

The tape shall be identified for being coal tar based. This shall be done by procedure as given in Annex C. 8 OTHER TESTS

In addition to the routine tests as specified in 7, the tape shall also be subjected to the following tests at least once in a yew a) b) Cathodic disbanding Microbiological test as per Annex D, and

tests as per Annex E.

9 PACKING 9.1 A suitable film separator shall be applied to the finished tape to prevent different layers of tape in a roll from sticking to each other. The film separator shall however be removed prior to application of tape.

IS 15337:2003 9.2 Unless otherwise specified, the tape shall be supplied in card board boxes suitably packed to prevent it from any damage or deterioration during transit, 9.3 The primer shall be suitably packed in 20 Iitres capacity steel drums. 10 HANDLING, TRANSPORTATION STORAGE OF COATED PIPES The contractor shall load, unload, pile the coated pipes within the suitable means to avoid damage to The owner shall approve such commencement of work. AND beat least 5 percent of the pipe length and minimum 3 in number support shall be provided. 11 MARKING 11.1 Each box and drum shall be legibly and indelibly marked with following information: a) b) c) d) Manufacturer's Batch/Lot Month/Year name and/or trade-mark, and

number, of manufacturing,

transport and stock coating plant using the pipe and coating. procedure prior to

Any other information relating to retention of quality of the tape at the customer's end including guidelines regarding storage of the tapes and primer. Marking

Coated pipes may be handled by means of slings of belts of proper width (minimum 60 mm) made of nonabrassive/non-metallic materials. The pipes shall be stacked completely clear from the ground at least 300 mm so that bottom row of pipes remain free from any surface water. The pipes shall be stacked at a slope so that draining rain does not collect inside the pipe. The lorries used for transportation shall be equipped with adequate pipe supports having as many round hollow beds as there are pipes to be placed on the bottom of the lorry bed. ANNEX A (Clause 6)
APPLICATION A-1 APPLICATION OF WRAPPING TAPE OF WRAPPING TAPES

A-1.l The surface of the pipe shall be thoroughly cleaned and shall be free of dirt, grease, oil rust, scale or other foreign matter. It shall also be thoroughly dried before application of primer. The pipe shall be cleaned by any one of the following methods as mutually agreed: a) Grit/shot blasting with suitable combination of grits and shots to obtain dense angular surface profile, and Mechanical cleaning. 4

b)

A-1.l.l All the oil and grease present on the metal surface, should be removed using a suitable solvent or cleaning rags before grit shot blasting or mechanical cleaning. Any other foreign matter which cannot be removed by blasting or mechanical cleaning shall be removed by other suitable means. The surfaces of the exposed base metal presenting a greyish matter appearance except that slight shadows; streaks or discoloration caused by rust stains or mild scale oxides. Blasted surfaces which rust before applying the primer coat should be again cleaned by wire brushing or emery paper. If the rust formation is heavy,

IS 15337:2003 that is, if the pipes have been exposed overnight without priming, the same shall be re-blasted once again before priming. A-1.1.2 Adequate moisture separators should be used so as to remove oil and moisture from the air supply of the blasting unit effectively. A-1.1.3 After protected and dust that may till the tape is A-1.2 Priming A-1.2.1 Primer The primer shall be resin based containing unmodified chlorinated quantity of coal tar pitch of same making coal tar tape and have the per 3.4. synthetic primer rubber and small quality used for characteristics as A-1.3.3 If the tape is being applied in cold weather, the surface of the pipe shall be preheated until it is warm to the touch and the traces of moisture are also removed. The primer shall then be applied and allowed to dry. A-1.4 If required by the user, the surface of the coated pipe can be covered up with craft paper when the pipeline is exposed for more than 5 days to in open ultra violet (UV) light (sun light). This however shall not be mandatory. Blackness of the coated surface can be removed by the above methods which will reduce excessive heating of the coating arising out of absorption of solar radiation; particularly where sun is very strong and the coated pipe remains over ground for long. A-1.4.1 White Wash Composition Ingredient Water Boiled linseed oil Quick lime Salt Quantity 189 Iitre 3.86 Iitre 68 kg 4.5 kg cleaning the pipes shall be effectively maintained free from all oil, grease and fall on the pipes from outside sources wrapped. containing more coating compound with either a blow lamp or a gas flame to soften the coating compound. Care shall however be taken to ensure that the compound does not melt. The tape shall then be spirally wrapped while maintaining tension around the surface of the pipe. The tape shall be applied radially if the pipe diameter is large. The adhesion test shall be carried minimum 72 h of curing time. out only after

A-1.3.2 An overlap of 12.5 mm is recommended single wrapping.

The primer and the coal tar tape shall be compatible to each other and the primer shall pass the adhesion test as specified in 7.1. A-1.2.2 Single uniform coal of primer, compatible with the tape to be used and free from floods or runs, shall be applied immediately after pipe has been cleaned and dried. A-1.2.3 Primer coverage shall be such as to ensure Imaximum bond between the steel surface and the tape. A-1.2.4 Atmospheric conditions, type and coverage of primer determine the drying time. If the primer coat is found to be unsatisfactory, the pipe shall be primed again. A-1.3 Wrapping Take the tape rolls out of the packing boxes and leave in the sun for at least 30 min before application. The tape can be hot applied using a suitable and compatible primer. To prepare white wash the sequence of operation shall be: Mix salt and water, then slowly and simultaneously add linseed oil and quick lime. The ingredients shall be thoroughly mixed and the mixture then allowed to stand for 72 h before use.

ANNEX B (Clause 7.3)
DIRECT IMPACT TEST B-1 TEST PIECES Take two steel plates of 300 mm x 300 mm x 3 mm free from oil and grease. One side of each plate shall be blasted to uniform grey surface finish and shall be free from rust, mill scale or any other foreign matter. Apply one coat of primer to cover the surface of the steel plate properly. B-1.1 Priming Both test plates as specified in B-1 shall be primed using the coverage as recommended by the manufacturer. The primer shall be applied with a clean flat-bristle brush of 25 mm width. Plates shall be dried in horizontal position in a well ventilated room. B-1.2 The primed surface shall be coated with the tape as per recommendations of the manufacturer. B-2 CONDITIONING The plates shall be kept at a temperature between 25�C and 35�C for a period of at least 7 h before testing. B-3 PROCEDURE Each plate shall be supported on a true plane surface of a block of wood. A steel ball weighing 650 g, with a well polished spherical surface shall be dropped from a height of 2.45 m above the surface of the plate. The ball shall be dropped so as to strike the tape at a point at least 100 mm away from the edges of the plate. B-4 ASSESSMENT AND REPORTING

After impact, the coating shall be examined for evidence of shattering and loosening from the plate. After the removal of loose coating the area of the loosened coating shall be determined. If the disbonded area is less than 10000 mm2, the coating is accepted to have passed the test.

These bacterial adversely affect a bitumen tape; but coal tar tapes are not adtersely affected by these bacteria, so only, coal [ar tape is suitable for underground application. Coal tar tape has got mL[cb better adhesion than bitumen tape. For underground pipeline only coal tar tape (and not bitumen tape) shall be used.

The level of petrol shall be about 5 cm above the tape sample. Cover the mouth of the beaker with two layers of thick polythene sheets and tie these polythene sheets with a rubber band around the mouth of the glass beaker. Allow the beaker to stand at room temperature for 24 h without any disturbance. No stirring is to be done. Take the tape sample out of the beaker after 24 h and spread it on blotting papers on a table. Allow it to dry in the air for 4 h. Weigh the tape accurately again (say B)

D-3 SAMPLE PREPARATION D-3.1 Prepare one test plate, measuring at least 200 mm x 100 mm x 15 mm. Free the surface of the steel plate from all oil and grease, then blast it to a uniform steel grey finish, removing rust, scale and all other foreign matter so that the peak to trough profile is 50-75 microns. Prime it and coat it with tape coating material as per the manufacturer's guidelines. To ensure freedom from accidental damage test the prepared plate with the flaw detector (see D-1.6).
NOTE -- It is important to ensure that blasted steel surfaces are free from traces of previous coating materials and do not subsequently become contaminated with oil or grease.

D-1.6 Flaw Detector, fitted with a soft metallic bristled straight brush approximately 75 mm long and 6 mm wide with bristles 6 mm long, adjusted to provide a voltage of 10 kV, so arranged that the maximum short circuit current is not greater than 8 mA. D-1.7 Reference Electrode, saturated calomel type, constructed from glass or plastics with porous plug, of diameter less than 10 mm. D-1.8 Platinum Wire, of 0.8 mm diameter, one 75 mm length for each test site. 7

IS 15337:2003 D-3.2 Flaw Detection Examine the prepared plate for evidence of cracking by means of the flaw detector (see D-1.6). If the flaw detector is not equipped with voltage indication, set it to givea 12mmspark inairto asteelplate. Pass the flaw detector over the coated specimen at approximately 6 mm distance from the coated steel surface. ignore edge effects. D-4 PROCEDURE Affix two plastic tubes (see D-1.9) perpendicular to the coated surface using a suitable elastomeric adhesive (see D-1 .10). Place them at a minimum distance of 33 mm frum the panel ends and from each other with their centres on the centre line of the panel width. Leave overnight to allow the adhesive to cure fully. Drill a6 mmhole through the coating material (see D-1.11) to the metal surface in the centJe of each test site, as a predamaged area. Fill each plastic tube (see D-1.9) to a depth of approximately 50 mm with sodium chloride solution (see D-2.1) and connect the apparatus as shown in Fig. 1. Connect the voltmeter (see D-1.2) as shown in Fig. 2 and with the porous tip of the reference electrode (see D-1.7) placed within 10 mm of the hole in the coating material, adjust the variable resistor (see D-1.3) until the voltmeter leais �1 .500 V with respect to the calomel electrode. At intervals of 24 h record the voltmeter reading and adjust the variable resistor to correct any drift from the �1 .500 V setting.

IS 15337:2003 Continue the test for 28 days, maintaining the temperature at 30 ~ 5�C. After this period assess disbanding at both test sites by the method described in D-5. D-5 ASSESSMENT Remove the plastics tube from each test site and wipe along the surface of the coating using a lint free paper towel (see D-1.12) and cathode area material. Make two parallel incisions through the coating and 12.5 mm apart across the panel so as to include the predamaged area. The cuts should extend 50 mm on each side of the predamaged area. Using a square ended pellets knife insert it into the centre portion of the predamaged area, between the parallel cuts, down to the metal. Using a gentle levering action, lift the strip of coating, if possible, with a slow peeling action and then grip the coating between the blade and thumb and continue the peeling action until the coating breaks. Repeat the peeling test in the opposite direction and then repeat the procedure at an angle of 90� to the first test. Apply one spot of phenolphthalein acid/base indicator (see D-2.2) to the exposed metal surface at the outside edge and allow it to flow towards the predamaged area. The purple boundary indicates the extent of disbanding. D-6 REPORTING Report the extent of disbanding as the radius in millimetres from the edges of the predamaged areas. Alternatively, if the coating is strongly adhering to the steel substrate, take the average distance at which the coating breaks as the extent of disbanding. The extent of disbanding shall not be more than 5 mm radius from the edge of the 6 mm holiday.

ANNEX E (Clause 8)
MICROBIOLOGICAL CORROSION RESISTIVITY TEST AGAINST SULPHATE REDUCING AND SULPHUR OXIDIZING BACTERIA RESPONSIBLE FOR CORROSION OF UNDERGROUND STEEL PIPELINES E-1 INTRODUCTION E-1.l It is well known that micro-organisms are closely involved in the transformation of elemental iron comprising the major material of iron and steel pipes. E-1.2 Bacteria mostly inhabitants in the soil are able to oxidize ferrous iron into ferric state which precipitates later as hydroxide of ferric iron. E-1.3 In the soil a variety of acids are formed by microbial action which may include sulphuric, nitric and a good number of organic acids and these may bring about the iron into soluble state. E-1.4 Also under increased anaerobic conditions in the soil or in aquatic environment, sulphides are formed from sulphates and organic sulphur compounds present in soil and iron may be precipitated in nature by ironoxidising bacteria. E-2 MICRO-ORGANISMS E-2.1 The micro-organisms belonging to two groups, namely Thiobacillus and Desulfovibrio are: 9 a) b) c) d) Thiobacillus Thiobacillus Thiobacillus Desulfovibrio Thio-oxidans; Ferro-oxidans; Thioparus; and Desulphuricans

Of these, bacteria at (a) and (c) are known to oxidize suiphur present in soil and produce sulphuric acid as one of the end products. The bacteria belonging to (b) and (d) are predominant in moist or submerged soil and are known to reduce sulphates or organic sulphur containing compound finally producing hydrogen sulphide. Thiobacillus Ferro-oxidans have however properties to oxidize reduced sulphur compounds and also elemental sulphur and iron. E-3 SCOPE OF TEST The sulphur oxidizing and sulphate reducing bacteria are mostly auto-tropic, that is, they do not require any complex organic food for their growth in soi I and water basins. Their habitat provides nutrition for their

IS 15337:2003 existence and activity. Therefore, it is necessary to determine the methods for retarding and inhibiting the growth and development of the different categories of bacteria (living in soil environment) as stated above. The aim is to prescribe standard methods of testing the presence of micro-organisms in soil substrata and then to check that the coal tar tape (with which the steel pipes are coated and protected) is not attacked by these bacteria or it retards and inhibits the growth of these bacteria in soil environment. E-6.2 Test for Sulphur Oxidizing Bacteria The bacteria of this group are autotropic and they either oxidize or reduce sulphur compounds obtaining their carbon from carbon dioxide of air. They could produce acid during their metabolism and are the principal agents of iron corrosion in soil. The common forms of the bacteria, namely, Thiobacillus Thioparus; and Thiobacillus Thio-Oxidans oxidize sulphur compounds. E-6.2.1 For Thiobacillus Thioparus in the autoclave at 15 psi for 20 min or in the hot air oven at 150�C for 1 h. b) Dissolve the following chemicals in distilled water in order of sequence to prepare the culture medium: Ammonium Magnesium Monobasic sulphate sulphate heptahydrate potassium phosphate : 0.2 g : 0.5 g : 3.0 g : 0.25 g : 0.01 g : 11

Calcium chloride Ferrous sulphate Distilled water to make the volume up to c)

E-6.2.1.1 Culture media and procedure
a)

Sterilize 250 ml conical flasks with stopper in the autoclave at 15 psi for 20 min or in the hot air oven at 150�C for 1 h. Dissolve the following chemicals in distilled water in order of sequence to prepare the culture medium: Sodium thiosulphate Dibasic potassium Magnesium Ammonium Manganese Calcium chloride chloride sulphate Ferric chloride hexahydrate Distilled water to make the volume up to pentahydrate phosphate : 10 g :2g : 0.1 g : O.lg : O.lg : 0.02 g : 0.02 g :11 d)

Weigh 10 g of sublimed sulphur in 250 ml conical flasks and add to it 100 ml of the culture medium; sterilize the flasks in the steam at atmospheric pressure at 100"C for 30 min for three successive days. This can be done by operating the autoclave keeping its nuts loose. Then steam will be escaping through the gap between the two halves of the autoclave. Sterilization is carried out for 3 successive days to kill spores. Inoculate the flasks containing the medium with 10-20 ml of soil suspension (1: 10) and incubate at 20 �C-300C for 4 to 5 days.

b)

E-6.2.2.2 Results The sulphur sinks to the bottom of flasks and the reaction of medium decreases the pH to 2.0 and the medium becomes turbid due to bacterial growth. These are likely to be present at the bottoms of water ways, canals and waste drainage of industrial installations also. Particularly moist soils with above bacteria are to be collected. E-7.2 Procedure E-7.2.1 Prepare three test pieces of steel pipes coated with the tape. The steel pipes will be of 40 mm NB and 150 mm length and are to be covered with the tape completely from all sides. E-7.2.2 Prepare 16 tape pieces as strips each of 25 mm width and 50 mm long.

procedure

Sterilize 250 ml conical flasks with stopper

11

IS 15337:2003 E-7.2 .3 Toensure freedom from accidental damage, test each sample piece with an electrical insulation detector. If the detector is not equipped with voltage indication, setitto givea 12mmspark inairtoasteei plate. Pass the detector over the specimen at approximately 6 mm distance from the tape surface. Edge effects are to be ignored. E-7.2.4 Prepare soil mixtures in two sets as follows: a) One set containing 5 parts (w/w)of bacteria free moist soil (containing 10-15 percent water) and 1 part (w/w) of moist soil containing Thio.bacillus Thio-Oxidans and Thiobacillus Thioparus. Let this mixture be called Mixture A. (Soil dried in air at room temperature will always have 10-15 percent of water.) Another set containing 5 parts (w/w) of bacteria free moist soil and 1 part (w/w) of moist soil containing Thiobacillus FerroOxidans and Desulfovibrio Desulphuricans. Let this mixture be called Mixture B. Sterilize all of them at 15 psi for 20 min. Add 0.10 ml of diluted soil suspension (1 part of Mixture A and 10 parts water) of Mixture A in 4 flasks. In the balance 4 flask add bacteria free soil in the same way as Mixture A. b) Take 100 ml of the specific media (see E-6.2.1) for the bacteria present in Mixture B in each of the 8 conical flasks of 250 ml volume. Sterilize all of them at 15 psi for 20 min. Add 0.10 ml of diluted soil suspension (1 part of Mixture B and 10 parts water) of Mixture Bin 4 flasks. In the balance 4 flasks add bacteria free soil in the same way as Mixture B. All the flasks are kept at 25"C-30"C in the incubator. Thereafter the cultures are to be examined after 28 days. After this period if there are positive growths, then the media in the flasks are ready for inoculation of tapes. The tape strips are then put into the media in the flasks (one strip in each flask). After another 62 days of incubation the tapes are to be taken out for assessment as mentioned in E-7.3.

c)

b)

Each soil mixture is to be mixed thoroughly and the moisture content is to be maintained at a level of 30-40 percent approximately. The three polyethylene jars are filled with the soil mixtures in the following manner and each of the three covered steel pipes is to be pressed into moist soil in such a manner that 3/4 of the total length is buried in all the three cases, namely Mixture A, Mixture B and the bacteria free moist soil. Moisture level is to be checked and water is to be added if required. All the three jars are to be kept in the incubation chamber maintained at 25"C-30"C. The pipes are to be carefully withdrawn after 90 days for examining the surface of the tape. In case the level of liquid medium goes down, sterilized water should be added from time to time to maintain the volume as before. Carry out the assessment as per E-7.3.

In case the level of liquid medium goes down, sterilized water should be added from time to time to keep the volume as before. E-7.3 Assessment E-7.3.1 The surface of the covered pipes (removed from the jars as referred in E-7.2.4 are to be cleaned with water and examined as to whether any spots have appeared or there are bacterial growth on the surface. The test with bacteria free soil shall give no spot of growth and acts as a reference. Compared to this reference other two wrapped pipes are to be examined. Even if there are 4-5 shallow spots, it will mean that the tape covering the steel pipes are resistant to attack by the micro-organisms present in the soil. E-7.3.2 After 90 days of incubation, the tape strips are to be taken out of the flasks and washed for examination. Compare with the reference strips (that is the samples tested with bacteria free soil) the other strips are to be examined. Even if there are 4-5 shallow spots, it will mean that the tapes are resistant to attack by micro-organisms present in the soil. A magnifying glass having 10 X magnification be used for locating spots on the tape. may

E-7.2.5 The enriched bacteria culture in a specific liquid and culture media is prepared by adding the Mixtures A and B and the effects on the tapes when dipped in the liquid cultures are examined. a) Take 100 ml of the specific media (see E-6.1.1) for the bacteria present in Mixture A in each of the 8 conical flasks of 250 ml volume.
